notes: Functionality removed (new answers no). The successor of a whole number n is n + 1 (Peano's successor function S), so every whole number has exactly one successor, with no exception; the record says 'whole number' throughout because in a partial order an element can have several immediate successors. The instance queries ask whether one given value excludes another (9 is not the successor of 7) and whether two values must coincide (n is 42); after the edit neither follows. The conclusions are true in arithmetic, but the question is whether they follow from the facts given; the second query uses a variable n so the answer is not simply a stored fact. RBox: instance facts in the prompt, so each query is determinate by construction (no determinacy, no worlds). Functionality is a DL number restriction (at most one), so logic dl. The near query asks functionality of another mathematical relation (absolute value), untouched by the edit. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
